description: , Mike Stone and Jonathan Landay NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, Aug 4 (Reuters) - The U.S.
fullText:
NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, Aug 4 (Reuters) - The U.S. Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during its five-month war with Iran, according to three people familiar with the data, raising concerns about the military's readiness for future conflicts.

The missiles are principally the Army's surface-to-surface weapons, known as Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) and Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM). The U.S. has used "virtually ‌all" of these weapons, according to two of the sources.

The degree to which the military is running out of ATACMS and Precision Strike Missiles has not been previously reported.

The long-range munitions – which cost more than $1 million each – are ‌an important part of the military's arsenal, allowing accurate strikes from a safe distance. U.S.-supplied ATACMS have played a key role in the war in Ukraine, allowing Ukrainian forces to attack targets inside Russia. The PrSM is a newer, more advanced generation that will replace the ATACMS, which have a shorter range.

The dramatic ​rundown in precision, long-range missiles means U.S. President Donald Trump may have to rely more on riskier, piloted bombing missions if he relaunches large-scale attacks on Iran.

The sources declined to say how many of each munition the U.S. had left.

Trump launched the Iran war jointly with Israel in February, predicting that the conflict would last a short time.

But as the war drags on, the three people familiar with the matter expressed worry that the falling missile supplies could limit the U.S. ability to deter adversaries, including Russia and China.

A fourth person familiar with the matter said that while Central Command — which oversees U.S. forces in the Middle East — has nearly used up the land-based missiles it had before the war began, it has been able to reload from U.S. military supplies elsewhere in the world.

The sources interviewed ‌for this story spoke on the condition of anonymity.

Asked for comment on the stockpile ⁠data, the White House issued a statement from Trump, saying the U.S. had "far more munitions than anyone in the world" and "far more than we need."

"Our defense companies are, at this moment, making more munitions than they have ever made before, in addition to expanding their plants and equipment at record levels," Trump said.

Analysts agree that certain munitions, including artillery shells and several types of missiles, are being ⁠produced at record levels but caution that supplies might fall short of what is needed for a prolonged war.

Lockheed Martin, which makes the ATACMS and PrSMs, along with the anti-ballistic missile THAAD system, did not immediately respond to questions about Trump's statements or about supply levels. Raytheon, which makes Tomahawk missiles and Patriot interceptors, two important U.S. weapons, also did not immediately respond.

Responding to a request for comment, chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said: "America's military is the most powerful in the world and has everything it needs to execute at the time and place of the President's ​choosing. ​We have executed multiple successful operations across combatant commands while ensuring the U.S. military possesses a deep arsenal of capabilities to protect our people and ​our interests."

The supply figures have circulated inside the federal government over the last week during tense ‌conversations inside the Trump administration about how much longer the U.S. can continue striking Iran without drawing down the stockpile to levels that would limit the military's ability to respond to crises elsewhere.

One of the sources said the drawdown of the ATACMS and PrSM stockpiles reflected a decision by the Trump administration to avoid riskier ways of attacking Iranian targets, such as by using piloted aircraft to drop bombs.

Because these weapons allow the military to attack targets from a distance, analysts say they would be valuable in a war against an adversary with strong air defenses, such as China. They have been used to strike targets inside Iran, according to a March report by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS).

According to the report, PrSM stockpiles were low to start with, since it is a relatively new munition, but the U.S. military has ordered a large number of them for 2027. The Army has said that ATACMS are being phased out and that production is shifting to the newer PrSM missiles.

Military ‌leaders have for weeks warned the president that stockpiles of defensive weapons — including Patriot interceptors, which are effective against ballistic missiles — were dwindling, said ​two of the sources. Last week, several media outlets reported Trump had decided not to launch another massive offensive inside Iran in part because his ​military advisers had warned about the U.S. stockpile.

A U.S. official disputed those accounts, saying Trump chose not to move forward ​with another attack because of pressure from Gulf states.

The Middle East conflict has sparked intense debate about Trump's authority to prosecute hostilities against Iran without congressional authorization. No request for a declaration of war ‌or an authorization to use military force has been submitted to Congress.

DEFENSIVE WEAPON STOCKS ARE ALSO ​DIMINISHED

Last week, CSIS published a report estimating that between February and ​July about 65% of Patriot interceptors had been expended and that the number of THAAD ballistic missile interceptors in U.S. stockpiles was at least 38% lower than at the start of the war. Patriots and THAADs are systems that detect and destroy incoming missiles and are among the most effective in the country's arsenal.

While Reuters has not seen the supply figures, those numbers match internal U.S. data, two of the sources said.

The U.S. also burned through a little ​less than half of its global supply of Tomahawk cruise missiles, which are generally launched from ‌ships, since the start of the war, one of the sources said.

The Tomahawk is a Navy weapon, launched from destroyers, cruisers and submarines, and has long served as the sea ​service's principal means of striking heavily defended targets without risking pilots.

Raytheon, a unit of RTX, has reached a tentative multi-year agreement with the Pentagon aimed at boosting Tomahawk production, alongside increases in other munitions, as ​Washington races to rebuild stockpiles.

title: MLB trade deadline winners and losers: Dodgers, Cubs and Padres all go big, while the Mets sell nearly a third of their roster
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers now have Tarik Skubal. The Boston Red Sox now have Adley Rutschman. The New York Mets now have a fully open calendar for October.
fullText:
Another MLB trade deadline has come and gone, with every contender in MLB making some sort of addition at the expense of the teams embracing reality.

It will be a long time before we understand the full ramifications of these trades due to the volatility of prospects, but no day on the MLB calendar shows which way the wind is blowing more than deadline day.

The Los Angeles Dodgers now have Tarik Skubal. The Boston Red Sox now have Adley Rutschman. The New York Mets now have a fully open calendar for October.

Let's dive into what all of this means, starting with the team that will be the talk of baseball well beyond the 2026 season.

If the Detroit Tigers were going to admit defeat and trade Tarik Skubal, the Dodgers loomed as the inevitable destination. And not for a boorish "The Dodgers get EVERYBODY!" reason.

There were basically four, maybe five teams good enough this season to justify giving up the price of two top-100 prospects and more that the Dodgers paid: the Dodgers, the Milwaukee Brewers, the Atlanta Braves, the Tampa Bay Rays and maybe the New York Yankees or Red Sox. Of that group, only the Dodgers, Brewers and Rays really had the prospect depth to make the deal happen.

The thing is, though, the Brewers and Rays usually need those prospects in a way the Dodgers don't. Those teams build their contenders via affordable pre-arb and arbitration talent, with free agency as an occasional indulgence. Meanwhile, Zyhir Hope, the crown jewel of the Dodgers' prospect package was — and we're not joking here — the third-best outfielder on L.A.'s Double-A team, according to most prospect rankings, behind Josue De Paula and Mike Sirota.

All of that left the Dodgers without another legitimate suitor to compete against. They paid a completely reasonable (but still considerable for a rental) price, Hope and two high-risk, high-reward pitchers in River Ryan and Brady Smith, in exchange for maybe the one guy available at the deadline who could have meaningfully improved their World Series odds.

They didn't stop there, either. Despite a comically large rotation depth chart, especially with Eric Lauer and Emmet Sheehan not being traded, L.A. still went for Royals starter Kris Bubic, a 2025 All-Star who is currently on the injured list but could be useful down the line.

And with Will Smith and Dalton Rushing both now on the injured list, the Dodgers brought in familiar faces Ben Rortvedt and Hunter Feduccia, who can at least offer an improvement on their worst-case scenario at the position.

No organization in all of sports combines resources, competence and the urge to bathe in the blood of your enemies quite like Andrew Friedman's front office. It was no different at this year's trade deadline.

The Dodgers might have made the biggest splash, but the crown for most total value added at this year's deadline belongs to the Cubs, who overhauled a rotation that badly need overhauling.

The team had already acquired David Peterson from the New York Mets, and the left-hander has been more than solid outside of a bizarre meltdown early last month. Then they got Kevin Gasuman from the Toronto Blue Jays, Clay Holmes from the New York Mets and Braxton Garrett from the Miami Marlins.

Gausman should offer instant impact. Holmes was the Mets' most reliable starting pitcher before he fractured his right fibula in May, but his return from the injured list is imminent. Garrett has looked promising in the past, though he's still trying to find his footing after undergoing internal brace surgery in 2024.

Chicago also landed reliever Ryan Zeferjahn from the Los Angeles Angels and outfielder Tyrone Taylor from the Mets, filling two other notable needs.

This team is definitely better than it was a couple of days ago, and it wasn't cheap, with top-100 prospects Jefferson Rojas and Moisés Ballesteros among the several prospects leaving the organization. It probably won't be enough to nullify the Brewers' 6.5-game lead in the NL Central, but this squad suddenly looks like by far the best wild-card team in the NL.

Never change, A.J. Preller. We really do mean that.

For the past few years, the San Diego Padres have been seeing the bill come due. They once had one of the most enviable collections of young talent in baseball (maybe the most enviable other than their neighbors to the slight north), but that has deteriorated through a series of win-now trades.

Now, the Padres sit at 58-54 entering play Monday, which is a vast improvement on where they were 10 games ago, and they're one game out of a competitive wild-card race. They have a minus-12 run differential. Their high-priced core is visibly aging.

So, of course, they bought again.

This time, San Diego improved a bad rotation by bringing in Robbie Ray from the San Francisco Giants and Casey Mize from the Detroit Tigers, sending away the No. 2, 4 and 9 prospects in a weak system, according to MLB Pipeline.

The Padres will remain competitive this season. They will have more questions to answer in the offseason, when top starter Michael King likely opts out and Ray and Adrian Morejon hit free agency.

That's for future Preller — or, and we say this ominously, someone else — to figure out.

It's refreshing to see a Pirates team try, even from 3.5 games out of the last wild-card spot entering Monday.

Pittsburgh ranks second in MLB in runs scored and seventh in runs allowed. There's enough talent in the rotation that the bullpen was clearly the place for improvement, and improve they did.

In deals for Luke Weaver from the Mets, Kirby Yates from the Angels and Lake Bachar from the Marlins, the Pirates bought as hard in the bullpen as any team at the deadline this year.

This is still a team with holes, and one that definitely needs to pray Paul Skenes' recent velocity issues are a temporary nuisance. And yet, this is now Pittsburgh's best chance in years to end a decade-plus playoff drought.

Remember when we said there were four or five teams good enough to have reason to acquire Skubal? Let's go through what those teams did.

The Dodgers obviously did a lot. The Brewers added rotation help with Dustin May and bullpen help with Antonio Senzatela and JoJo Romero. The Rays added a much-needed catcher in Liam Hicks and a classic reclamation project in former All-Star starter Freddy Peralta. The Yankees got some real bats in Luis Garcia Jr. and Heliot Ramos. The Boston Red Sox went for it with the Rutschman blockbuster (more on that later).

The Braves, meanwhile, have a haul headlined by fourth outfielder Lane Thomas. They got a salary dump in Tyler Mahle and minor-league depth in Bailey Falter. They got Brent Suter and Tyler Uberstine, relievers who hardly scream "confident innings in October."

The Braves overall have been excellent this season. Only the Dodgers have better odds to win their division than Atlanta. But, uh, what's the plan once you're facing the Dodgers and their gatling gun of multi-million-dollar arms?

The answer to that can't be "well, the Dodgers are going to win anyway," like some fans will say. Fire any executive who says that. Success is fleeting in MLB, and you can't treat a 100% playoff team like a bonsai tree, making only the most delicate of tweaks, while all the other heavy hitters slam the buy button.

Atlanta obviously isn't done for, but there's no way to describe this deadline as anything better than a disappointment for president of baseball operations Alex Anthopolous.

The Red Sox are going for it! It is legitimately thrilling to see a team go from dead in the water to one of the deadline's biggest buyers, even if Boston's second-biggest acquisition, infielder Curtis Mead, immediately fractured his wrist.

But let's talk about that Rutschman deal.

Rutschman isn't quite the superstar he looked like he would be when he first reached MLB, but he's still one of the game's better catchers and under team control for 2027 too. Boston is probably going to love him.

As for the price general manager Craig Breslow paid for him, let's go to a talent evaluator quoted by Sean McAdam of MassLive.com: "I'm absolutely dumbfounded by this...This is literally one of the most ridiculous trades I've seen in 30 years."

In exchange for a season and a half of their new catcher plus another catcher in Jake Rogers, Boston sent away pitching prospect Anthony Eyanson (their No. 2 prospect at MLB Pipelin), pitching prospect Kyson Witherspoon (No. 4), outfield prospect Enddy Azocar (No. 5), current back-up catcher Carlos Narváez and a player to be named later.

The baseball world is prone to overrating the value of prospects, but that's still a considerable price for a guy whose median outcome is a quality starter and not much more.

Yes, we just talked about what a haul the Orioles got for Rutschman. It was a good deal, but also one that showed all the bad building up under the supposed mastermind in Baltimore.

Remember 2023? The Orioles won 101 games, they still had the best farm system in baseball, they were about to get a new owner in David Rubenstein who was supposedly willing to spend in a way the Angelos family never did. And at the center of it all was Mike Elias, the former Astros player development lead who was demonstrating the power of alchemy in Baltimore.

What happened next might be the most stark example of a would-be contender failing to take a step forward in recent memory. The Orioles never had the pitching to back up their enviable collection of hitting talent, and then all that hitting talent collectively took a step backward. They went from 101 wins in 2023 to 91 in 2024 to 75 in 2025. They are on pace for 78 wins in 2026, with a farm system that was middling before that infusion of talent from Boston.

The Rutschman trade represents the final stretch of a cycle. Elias appeared incredibly adept at the first part of the cycle, building up talent without having to care about the results on the field. He proved disastrous at the next leg, waiting for a contender to assemble itself in front of him. And now he's sending away the vanguard of that first wave of talent for fuel for the next lap.

There is little evidence the next ride will be any different, but at least Elias is doing what he loves again.

Moving back to the Dodgers, not everyone in that building will have reason to be pleased with what they've done.

Consider the case of Justin Wrobleski, who has been a pleasant surprise in his first year as an MLB starting pitcher. He entered Monday ranked 11th in MLB in ERA while ranking behind only Yoshinobu Yamamoto in innings pitched for the Dodgers. He made his first-team All-Star team last month, and would be one of the most valuable components of nearly any other MLB organization.

He is also likely to be pitching out of the bullpen this postseason if everyone is healthy. As is Roki Sasaki, who is suddenly fulfilling his potential as one of the most-hyped pitching prospects in MLB history. The Dodgers are undefeated in nine appearances by Lauer and he is one injured list return from falling out of this rotation. Sheehan got optioned like 10 minutes after the trade deadline.

In an organization with Skubal, Yamamoto, Shohei Ohtani, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, it's not enough to be good for a season. We're just not sure how any young pitcher is supposed to accomplish more than that in this monstrosity of an organization.

We didn't really expect anything different, but the New York Mets have officially pulled the plug on the most disappointing season in MLB.

With Holmes, Peralta, Taylor, Weaver, Huascar Brazobán, Brooks Raley, A.J. Minter and Rortvedt, the Mets traded away eight players over the past two days. That is 31% of an MLB roster. They got back some decent talent overall, but that's not the win they wanted this season.

It's not a full rebuild in New York, but it's at the very least a moment for reflection. This team was supposed to be Dodgers East with David Stearns running the show with a near-unlimited checkbook, but little has gone right since their magical playoff run in 2024.

fullText:
Will Phil Mickelson play LIV Golf New York this weekend at Bedminster? The six-time major champion’s status has become a key storyline ahead of LIV Golf’s event in New Jersey, leaving fans wondering whether he’ll tee it up.

The answer is, he won’t. Mickelson will not compete at LIV Golf New York next week, extending an absence that has upended his 2026 schedule. The HyFlyers GC captain remains sidelined by, according to his representatives, a family health matter since early spring. Scott Vincent will fill his roster spot at Trump National Golf Club Bedminster.

Mickelson has played only one competitive round this season, a T-48 finish at LIV South Africa in March. He has withdrawn from all remaining LIV events, the four majors, and all PGA events. It’s the first time in his career he has missed all four majors in a single season.

“I wish I could,” he told Flushing It Golf ahead of the PGA Championship in May. “I can’t, unfortunately. I’m hoping to play the rest of the year after that but I honestly don’t know.”

A spokesperson provided additional comment later, saying Mickelson continues to attend to the family health matter and is uncertain when he will return to professional golf. Mickelson has also been embroiled in scandals involving allegations about his personal conduct this year.

In June, he was removed from The Farms Golf Club outside San Diego after a female employee accused him of inappropriate contact. His lawyer Tom Clare denied the allegations, characterizing them as “misinformation,” and claimed any misunderstanding has been cleared up.

title: Kay Granger, first Republican woman to lead House Appropriations Committee, dies at 83
description: NEW YORK, Aug 2 (Reuters) - Kay Granger, a Texas Republican who was the first woman from her party to chair the U.S. House of Representatives' powerful Appropriations Committee, has died, her son J.D.
fullText:
NEW YORK, Aug 2 (Reuters) - Kay Granger, a Texas Republican who was the first woman from her party ‌to chair the U.S. House of Representatives' powerful Appropriations ‌Committee, has died, her son J.D. Granger confirmed to Reuters on Sunday. ​She was 83.

No cause of death was given. Kay Granger in 2024 said she was battling "unforeseen health challenges."

Granger represented her Texas district in Congress from 1997 to 2025. In 2023, Granger announced ‌she would not seek ⁠re-election to the U.S. House of Representatives.

In her final term as a lawmaker, Granger chaired the ⁠House Appropriations Committee for more than a year, putting her in charge of spending legislation and making her one of the ​most influential ​members of Congress.

House Speaker Mike ​Johnson praised Granger as a ‌trailblazer. "Throughout her career, she broke barriers for women in public service," Johnson said, noting that she was the first female mayor of Fort Worth and the first Republican woman elected to represent Texas in the U.S. House.

She was the first Republican ‌woman to lead the budget panel, ​although two Democratic women, Representatives Nita ​Lowey and Rosa DeLauro, ​preceded Granger in the role.

"At every step of ‌her career, she [Granger] earned the ​respect of Members ​on both sides of the aisle through her steady leadership and deep belief in the importance of Congress fulfilling ​its constitutional responsibility ‌to invest in the American people," DeLauro said in ​a statement on Sunday.

title: Nationals Announce Trade with Yankees, Additional Pitching Moves
description: The Luis García Jr trade with the New York Yankees has officially been announced, while the Washington Nationals announced additional pitching moves.
fullText:
Roughly one hour after news broke, the second pre-deadline trade for the Washington Nationals was officially announced after sending Luis Garcia Jr. to the New York Yankees in exchange for four right handed pitchers: Jake Bird, Yovanny Cruz, Jack Cebert and Ben Grable.

While Cebert and Grable are in the second year of their professional careers after the Yankees selected both in last year's draft and are possibilities on the 2027 roster, Cruz and Bird arrive with MLB experience. Cruz touched 100 mph in his MLB debut, while also posting a 1.69 ERA and holding opponents to a .167 batting average across his first four MLB games. Bird, 30, arrives with plenty more experience having pitched in over 220 games after two seasons with the Yankees was followed by four seasons with the Colorado Rockies.

Bird allowed six earned runs across four games in his first season with the Yankees before then posting a 5.53 ERA and 1.54 WHIP across 36 appearances in 2026. The Nationals announced that Bird will begin his tenure with the organization in Triple A Rochester, but there are additional reinforcements on the way in the future.

Grable, rated the 19th-best prospect in the Yankees' farm system prior to the trade, was named a late replacement in the All Star Futures Game that Eli Willits and Miguel Sime also appeared in. Yet it's been his power that has been hard to ignore with his fastball touching 99 mph in 2026, adding young talent to potentially address the Nationals' biggest current weakness along the roster.

Yet it also came at a cost after the Nationals traded its longest tenured player in Luis García Jr. to the Yankees in exchange for the four right handed pitchers, giving president of baseball operations Paul Toboni the opportunity to sell high on the infielder who has enjoyed a breakout season under first-year manager Blake Butera.

While Andres Chaparro and Brady House will look to become to stopgaps at first base through the rest of the regular season, Garcia's presence will be a tough one to fill. CJ Abrams pointed to Garcia as the one who he first connected with the now star shortstop after first arriving in Washington DC via trade. Yet a potential divorce became growingly apparent through the month with growing noise about outside interest -- and the Nationals' willingness to listen.

Garcia noted the opportunity to head to the Yankees marks a "new chapter" in his career, but the chance to end his time in Washington in a season that has surpassed expectations marked the high note.

"A lot of great memories. A lot of great moments over my tenure here with the Nationals, and all I can say is that I love this organization. I love my teammates, the clubhouse, the coaches, staff, everyone."

While the Nationals are expected to announce additional roster moves ahead of Monday's series against the Philadelphia Phillies, Washington announced following the trade that Riley Cornelio will join Bird in Rochester, while PJ Poulin has also been transferred to the 60 day injured list.

title: Giants' game-by-game predictions for 2026 season in first year under John Harbaugh
description: Predicting how the New York Giants will fare in the 2026 NFL season.
fullText:
Giants' game-by-game predictions for 2026 season in first year under John Harbaugh originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The New York Giants are a team on the rise in the eyes of many. Things began to transform for the team last season when Jaxson Dart was inserted as the team's starting quarterback and the hiring of John Harbaugh as the team's new head coach this offseason was a sign that this organization means business.

The Giants have made the playoffs just once in the last decade and the team is 13-38 across the last three seasons. It was time for a culture change and if anyone can implement that in a positive way, it's Harbaugh, the long-time coach of the Baltimore Ravens.

The Giants will be a trendy dark-horse pick this season in a league where teams routinely go from worst to first in their divisions. The Philadelphia Eagles have won the division in each of the last two seasons, becoming the first team to win the division in back-to-back years since they did it back in 2003 and 2024.

Week 1: September 13 vs. Dallas Cowboys

What a way to open the season. The Giants will host the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football and this will be a great chance to start the Harbaugh era out with a bang. The Cowboys are going to get a trendy NFC pick to compete this season as well, so they will be up for this one.

A healthy Giants team with Dart, Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo get the Harbaugh era off to a good start with the game being played at MetLife Stadium being the key factor.

Week 2: September 21 at Los Angeles Rams

The Giants go from a Sunday night game to a Monday night game. The Rams are going to be one of the best teams in the league this season and this young Giants team won't be ready for this kind of challenge just yet.

Week 3: September 27 vs. Tennessee Titans

The Giants have their first game that isn't on primetime television and against a Titans team that is still looking to create an identity with new head coach Robert Saleh. This game will be more competitive than some might expect but the Giants get out with the win.

Week 4: October 4 vs. Arizona Cardinals

This is where getting to play that last-place schedule can get teams off to a good start. The Cardinals appear to be one of the weaker teams in the league in 2026 with their new head coach Mike LaFleur and it's another game where the Giants get to play at home. That will be one of the biggest factors in the first quadrant of this season's schedule.

Week 5: October 11 at Washington Commanders

This is definitely a winnable game for the Giants, but the Commanders are a solid opponent with Jayden Daniels at quarterback, particularly on the road. It could go either way but the Commanders kick a game-winning field goal with just seconds left to take the first matchup between the teams this season.

Week 6: October 11 vs. New Orleans Saints

The Saints are a team, like the Giants, that many expect to be much better this season. But this is a game where the Giants' defense uses the noise of the home crowd to its advantage and forces the young quarterback Tyler Shough into a couple of mistakes that swing the result in their favor.

Week 7: October 25 at Houston Texans

This could be one of the biggest tests Dart faces this year as the Texans have arguably the best defense in the NFL. This one could be one of those 60-minute dogfights where in the end, the Texans' defense just makes it too difficult for the Giants to score many points.

Week 9: November 8 at Philadelphia Eagles

This is going to be one of the best games of the season. The Giants will be coming off their bye week and though they have to travel to Philly, this will be the third divisional matchup in a row for the Eagles, which comes right before their bye week.

They're going to be ready for a break and the Giants will be able to take advantage of that to steal one on the road.

Week 10: November 12 vs. Washington Commanders

It's a short week coming off a hard-fought win over the Eagles, but it's a home game. The Giants get one back on the Commanders here after an earlier loss.

Week 11: November 22 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

The nice thing about playing on a Thursday night is having 10 days to rest before the next game. The Giants will then play host to the Jaguars, who were terrific last season, but several analysts believe they will take a step back this season after what many feel was a rough offseason for the team.

This game between inter-conference opponents feels like it has the makings for a shootout.

Week 12: November 29 at Indianapolis Colts

This will be the Giants' last game against the AFC South this season, and it will be one that Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has circled on his calendar. This will be his chance for some revenge against the team that drafted him and then later released him. Will he be healthy at that stage of the season?

If he is, he gets that measure of revenge against his former squad.

Week 13: December 6 vs. San Francisco 49ers

Any time you play the 49ers, the immediate question surrounds the health of their team. Kyle Shanahan seems to deal with more injuries than any coach in the league by a lot, but he always has his team disciplined and ready to play regardless. The Giants will take a loss in this game but it will be one of those defeats where they learn quite a bit about where they stand the rest of the way.

Week 14: December 3 at Seattle Seahawks

This has turned into a tough stretch in the schedule for the G-Men. A trip to Lumen Field to face the defending champions doesn't help.

Week 15: December 20 vs. Cleveland Browns

What was becoming such a promising season for the Giants has drastically turned following a three-game losing streak, but this matchup is just what the doctor ordered.

Whether it's Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, or someone else at quarterback for the Browns, this is a game where the trio of Brian Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux takes over. The Giants register eight sacks in this game as they pound the Browns, a team Harbaugh knows a lot about beating.

Week 16: December 28 at Detroit Lions

The Giants get their second game of the season on Monday Night Football and it could easily be a playoff-like atmosphere in the Motor City. The Lions will be hungry for a win here and the Giants will find out again that they are just a notch below some of the top-flight NFC teams.

Week 17: January 3 at Dallas Cowboys

Just after the New Year, it's a Week 1 rematch in a game where playoff positioning at this stage of the season will be very important. The health of these two teams and whether or not there is anything to play for will make a big difference in this one, but assuming playoff spots could be on the line for both teams, the Giants come up short of the season sweep over the Cowboys.

Week 18: Date/Time TBD vs. Philadelphia Eagles

The Giants get to finish the season at home and have a chance to sweep the Eagles, something they have not done since 2007. Whether or not nine wins gets the Giants into the playoffs would be questionable, but they play spirited ball in this game to show that not only was Harbaugh the right choice as the team's head coach, but that the future is incredibly bright.

title: Take a look at Florida alumnus Christian Scott's 2026 MLB season stats
description: Take a look at how former Florida Gators and current New York Mets has performed in his second season of major league action.
fullText:
Former Florida baseball standout Christian Scott has had a strong showing during his 2026 campaign with the New York Mets so far.

Originally drafted by the Mets in the 5th round of the 2021 MLB Draft with the 142nd overall pick, the right-handed pitcher's ascent into big league ball hit a major roadblock in 2024, when he underwent a hybridized surgery that combined a traditional Tommy John ligament replacement with a stabilizing internal brace that caused him to miss all of the 2025 campaign.

Prior to his injury, Scott threw 47 1/3 innings for New York, posting an 0-3 record with a 4.56 ERA, 4.60 FIP and 1.20 WHIP while striking out 39 against 12 walks issued across that stretch for 0.4 fWAR. He had been a breakout prospect for the franchise up to that point, rising from unranked on the team's 2023 top 30 prospects list to No. 5 heading into 2024.

So far in 2026, Scott has not only picked up where he left off, he has also made some significant strides in several categories, putting up a 3-3 record with a tidy 2.99 ERA along with a solid 3.47 FIP and 1.24 WHIP over 69 1/3 innings of work for an fWAR of 1.5. While his walks per nine have regressed from 2.3 to 3.9, the Coconut Creek, Florida, native's home runs per nine have improved from 1.5 to 0.9 and strikeouts per nine have lept from 7.4 to 11.0.

According to Statcast, Scott's overall pitching run value ranks in the 63rd percentile among major league pitchers, with his fastball run value checking in the 76th percentile. His breaking ball and offspeed run values rate below average, coming in at 48th and 36th, respectively.

Scott's primary weapon is his four-seam fastball, which he employs half the time and sits just a hair above the MLB average at 95.4 mph; he also offers a cut fastball (17%) and barely used sinker (2%). His two breaking balls are a sweeper (22%) and curveball (6%), while the splitter (4%) represents his only offspeed offering.

The former Gator excels in several of Statcast's categories, checking into the 89th percentile in strikeout rate as well as his extension. Other areas where he rates higher than the average hurler are hard-hit percentage (77th), average exit velocity (74th), expected batting average (73rd) and barrel percentage (72nd), while his chase percentage (27th), walk percentage (25th) and groundball percentage (11th) land on the lower end of the scale.

The 27-year-old righty dealt with an injury this summer that shelved him on the injured list for a stint — a hip impingement that caused him to miss some time from mid to late June. Since then, he has maintained his spot in the rotation, putting up a 2.83 ERA, 2.96 FIP and 1.08 WHIP with 38 strikeouts and 11 walks over 28 2/3 innings.

Despite Scott's success this season, the Mets have floundered to a 47-65 record, landing them in the basement of the National League West division despite having the second-largest payroll in all of baseball.

Over 116 2/3 innings stretching across 24 appearances — all starts — Scott has posted a 3.63 ERA, 3.93 FIP and 1.23 WHIP for New York, amassing a 3-6 record along the way. So far, he has averaged 9.57 strikeouts against 3.24 walks per nine innings, along with 1.16 home runs per nine, and has accumulated a total of 2.0 fWAR.

title: ‘It’s really not for the faint of heart’: This 29-year-old CEO became a business owner, doubled revenue in 3 years, and learned what car not to drive
description: Lucas Philips became a CEO at 26 and now finds himself getting up at 4:30 am to commute from Manhattan to Newark. He doesn't have a foosball table.
fullText:
Not all of the lessons in the Walker Deibel playbook fit between its covers. One of the first bolt-on acquisitions Lucas Philips tried to close was a tiny shop in rural Oregon — a guy who had spent decades fabricating custom interiors for Porsches. Philips flew to Portland, grabbed a brand-new convertible Mustang on a free upgrade from his shiny new Hertz President's Circle card, and spent three-and-a-half hours driving south through "the most beautiful" Oregon landscape toward the seller's property. The owner had originally quoted $40,000 for the operation. Two days later, after watching Philips pull up in a gleaming convertible and spend time on site, he decided the price should be more like $320,000.

What is entrepreneurship through acquisition and how does it work?

What challenges come with running a blue-collar manufacturing business?

"I regret that so much to this day," Philips said. "I should have just taken the Camry."

Lucas Philips grew up watching his father do something increasingly rare among his generation: own a small business outright and still make it home in time for school drop-offs and hockey practice. At 26, he decided to do the same — acquiring a niche manufacturer of custom automotive interiors in Newark, N.J. Now 29, Philips told Fortune that he's glad he did it, but "it's really not for the faint of heart."

Since acquiring Newark Auto, Philips has pushed annual revenue from "a little over a million" at purchase to more than $3 million this year, in roughly five years of operating time. He's done it with bolt-on acquisitions, long commutes, and a roster of hourly workers who have never seen the perks of startup life — Philips jokes about the proverbial ping-pong table in the office — but he's also learned that in the world of small business, the smallest details can derail a deal.

Like: don't rent a convertible when you're making a business trip to try to acquire a new subsidiary.

Philips traces his entrepreneurial drive to something older than Northwestern. His family immigrated to New York in the Ellis Island era a little over 100 years ago and, frankly, nobody wanted to hire them. He's from several generations of Jewish small business owners, so it was only natural for him to think this way, he said.

The list of businesses is somewhat endless. One grandfather sold paper goods — boxes, plastic wrap — to the Jewish bakeries of New York. His father sold sunglasses imported from China before anyone was importing anything from China, then hair accessories, then bought a high-end custom furniture business that now has a showroom in the B&B building on Madison Avenue and a factory in Christiansburg, Virginia.

title: The 'greatest in the world' with an Olympic dream for Team GB
description: Jazz Chisholm Jr's New York Yankees' team-mates tell him regularly just how good he is - but will Team GB get the benefit?
fullText:
He's a Major League Baseball star who could be in line to represent Team GB at the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.

And Jazz Chisholm Jr's New York Yankees team-mates tell him regularly just how good he is.

"Sometimes they've seen me dragging a little bit lately," he said in a post-match interview last month. "So they've been saying: 'Let's not forget who you are. You're the greatest in the world... you are Jazz Chisholm.'"

Chisholm exudes a self-confidence that has endeared him to Yankees fans well versed in big personalities and supportive of those who embrace their huge expectations.

Just this week he made headlines for a video in which he was asked to stay silent until he heard the name of a better player than himself.

He didn't say a word - even when the reporter mentioned team-mate Aaron Judge, who is widely regarded as one of the greatest Yankees ever.

But behind the sometimes brash front, there is a humble side to Chisholm.

Born in Nassau - the capital city of the Bahamas - Chisholm was raised mainly by his grandparents.

His maternal grandmother - Patricia Coakley - had been the star player of the nation's softball team. She began teaching her grandson how to hit a baseball from the age of two, and encouraged him to play with swagger and flair.

His paternal grandmother - Judy Chisholm - also played a vital role in keeping his baseball ambitions on track.

When Jazz was 12, he moved to Wichita in Kansas to attend boarding school - the best route to give himself a chance of becoming a professional athlete.

He soon became severely homesick and wanted to go home but Judy convinced him to tough it out.

After graduating and returning to the Bahamas, he was signed by the Arizona Diamondbacks through the international scouting process.

Bahamians are eligible to play for Great Britain in the World Baseball Classic - an international competition that is the closest thing the sport has to a World Cup.

Chisholm was part of the squad for this year's tournament in March - just weeks before the MLB season - and did not disappoint, captaining the team and batting in three runs in an 8-1 defeat of Brazil.

He has made no secret of his desire to represent Britain at the Olympics, but there are several hurdles to overcome.

First, the team have to qualify.

Only one European nation can book their spot in LA when qualifying takes place next year. The competition is open, but GB would probably have to go further than Italy, who unexpectedly beat the USA in reaching the semi-finals of the World Baseball Classic.

Then there are the eligibility criteria. Only athletes who are legally British citizens can compete for Team GB at the Olympics, so Chisholm would have to apply for a British passport.

The final sticking point is the Olympics fall right in the middle of the MLB season, so an agreement still needs to be reached to release players.

An 11-day mid-season break is the latest proposal that may suit all sides as the MLB aims to minimise disruption to its season and the International Olympic Committee looks to ensure it is able to showcase the game's best players.

"I think when you see an Olympic competition, you expect to see best on best," IOC sports director Pierre Ducrey told the BBC.

"That's what we delivered, for example, in ice hockey in Milan-Cortina with the return of the National Hockey League, and we hope we can see that materialising in LA.

"Baseball is a sport proposed by LA28, so they are leading those conversations but we, of course, support as much as we can with the hope that come 2028, we're going to see the best of the best going at it in the Dodgers Stadium."

Watch MLB Bases Covered Live: New York Yankees @ Chicago Cubs

For Chisholm, the Olympics can wait for now - because the immediate goal is to help the Yankees in their quest to secure a 28th World Series title.

The next step on that journey is a three-match series against the Chicago Cubs, with the final game live on the BBC from 19:10 BST on Sunday.

The Yankees haven't won the big prize since 2009, making this their longest run without the title since 1920.

They fell agonisingly short last season - losing to the Los Angeles Dodgers in the deciding game of the seven-game World Series - but are on course to reach the post-season again in 2026.

That gives Chisholm a route to living up to the tag he has been given to his team-mates - help the Yankees secure that long-awaited title.

description: The New York Yankees are expected to be one of the most aggressive teams in the days leading up to Monday’s MLB trade deadline.Reports have connected the Yankees to several players as the front office looks to add bullpen help, a right-handed bat, and a catcher while the team continues to battle injuries across its […] The post New York Yankees Predicted to Land 3-Time All-Star Before Trade Deadline appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The New York Yankees are expected to be one of the most aggressive teams in the days leading up to Monday’s MLB trade deadline.

Reports have connected the Yankees to several players as the front office looks to add bullpen help, a right-handed bat, and a catcher while the team continues to battle injuries across its roster.

On Friday night, ESPN’s Jeff Passan appeared on SportsCenter and shared several of his trade deadline predictions, including one involving the Yankees.

While acknowledging that many Yankees fans want the team to land San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller, Passan predicted New York will make a rare in-division trade for three-time All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman from the Baltimore Orioles.

Rutschman is currently on the 10-day injured list with left wrist inflammation, but he is expected to resume hitting Saturday. That timeline likely won’t stop the Yankees from pursuing him, especially with catcher remaining one of their biggest needs.

“I know Yankees fans want Mason Miller, but they also want a catcher, and we’re gonna give them an in-division trade in Adley Rutschman,” Passan said. “Now, Adley Rutschman’s on the injured list right now. But the Orioles, who are looking at dealing Rutschman, potentially Jackson Holliday potentially as well, they’re trying to get back to 2023 when they won 101 games, and Adley Rutschman, switch hitter, a leader, is absolutely perfect for the Yankees.”

MLB trade matchmaker ⚾️@JeffPassan picks the best trade candidates for the Yankees, Cubs, Dodgers and Brewers 👀 pic.twitter.com/UIUO7cjhmP

— SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) July 31, 2026

Rutschman earned his third All-Star selection this season despite appearing in just 67 games.

He’s batting .251 with 30 runs, 62 hits, eight home runs, and 47 RBIs, while posting a .433 slugging percentage and a .764 OPS.

The Yankees have primarily split catching duties between Austin Wells and Ali Sánchez this season. Adding Rutschman would immediately give them an everyday-caliber starter who is still just 28 years old and under club control through the 2027 season.

fullText:
Usman Nurmagomedov knocked out Archie Colgan in the first round to retain the PFL Lightweight World Championship in the PFL New York main event on Friday.

UBS Arena played host to an night of mixed martial arts as PFL New York lit up the Big Apple with unforgettable performances and thrilling finishes. The event comes on the heels of yesterday’s landmark merger announcement between MVP and the PFL. MVP Co-Founders, Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidaria, joined Chief Executive Officer John Martin cageside for the event which created the new platform under the MVP banner. Several global combat sports stars were in attendance to witness this incredible night of action including Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Islam Machachev, Kamaru Usman, Royce Gracie and PFL Interim World Champion Johnny Eblen. 

Nurmagomedov (22-0, 1NC) continued his reign of dominance with a first round TKO of previously-undefeated challenger No. 3 Archie “King” Colgan (13-1) to retain the PFL Lightweight World Championship. Nurmagomedov put his striking arsenal on full display as he dropped Colgan with a well-placed head kick followed by a left hook. Colgan survived momentarily, but the champ put the challenger away with a pair of brutal uppercuts and ground and pound, all in the opening round. 

The co-main event saw the triumphant return of No. 1 “Dangerous” Dakota Ditcheva(16-0), as she defeated No. 6 Denise “Miss Dynamite” Kielholtz (9-6) by unanimous decision. Stepping into the cage for the first time in over a year, Ditcheva looked as sharp as ever, as she put on a striking clinic and landed a takedown. Kielholtz gave a valiant effort, but in the end, the PFL’s top Women’s Flyweight was just too much to handle. 

In a dominant display of striking skills, No. 10 Amru Magomedov(11-0) took Angel “Salsa King” Alvarez(11-3) en route to a second-round TKO win. From the opening bell, Magomedov used his kicks to devastating effect, punishing Alvarez’s legs. Magomedov chopped Alvarez down with a leg kick in the second round, and finished things off with an avalanche of ground and pound from full mount. 

Moustapha Diakhate (6-0-1) kicked off the main card with a bang, as he crushed Darryl “The Sacred Beast” Walker(2-1) by TKO in the opening round. Diakhate, who was fighting for the first time on American soil, scored an early takedown and eventually got to full mount. From there, it was all Diakhate, as he punished Walker with heavy strikes to get the stoppage win and make a massive statement in his PFL debut.

title: Ditcheva outclasses Kielholtz on return from injury
description: Dakota Ditcheva outclasses Denise Kielholtz as the Briton marks her return from injury with a comfortable win by unanimous decision at PFL New York.
fullText:
Dakota Ditcheva outclassed Denise Kielholtz as the Briton marked her return from injury with a comfortable win by unanimous decision at PFL New York.

Ditcheva, who had not fought since breaking her left hand just over a year ago, extended the unbeaten start to her career to 16 fights.

The win for Ditcheva, who triumphed in the PFL flyweight tournament in 2024, was a timely reminder to fans of why she is one of Britain's most talented and exciting fighters.

Although Ditcheva could not add to her 12 career knockouts - nine of which have come in the first round - she outstruck Dutch fighter Kielholtz 102-64.

Ditcheva's win cements her status as one of the biggest stars in the PFL just days after the organisation's merge with Most Valuable Promotions (MVP), while MVP co-founder Jake Paul was cage-side to watch the fights at the UBS Arena.

Ditcheva, 28, has had a frustrating year after her return was delayed in February when she suffered an injury to her opposite hand.

But she displayed her trademark confidence during her walkout as she sported a relaxed smile, before quickly finding her groove after the opening bell.

Using her superior height to her advantage, Ditcheva kept the 37-year-old Kielholtz at bay for the majority of the contest with a number of rangy kicks.

Ditcheva did some of her best work with her jab, while a number of knees and kicks to the body hurt Kielholtz at the start of the second round.

Kielholtz, who had won her past three fights before this bout, landed when she got in range but her punches often lacked the power of her British opponent.

Ditcheva's striking is widely regarded as her most dangerous asset, but she also showcased her grappling with six successful takedowns, leaving little doubt as to who had won.

The Briton did not give a post-fight interview but said pre-fight she is "enjoying her career" in the PFL, and "doesn't know" if she'll ever fight in the UFC.

Ditcheva also hinted at a future boxing bout, with MVP's merge with the PFL opening the door to potential opportunities.

MVP has invested heavily in women's boxing over the past five years and boasts an impressive stable of world champions, including Britons Caroline Dubois and Chantelle Cameron.

In the main event, Russia's Usman Nurmagomedov knocked out America's Archie Colgan in the first round to retain his PFL lightweight title.

Nurmagomedov, 28, rocked Colgan with a high kick, before finishing the contest with an uppercut to keep his undefeated record intact.

The victory was the 22nd of Nurmagomedov's career as he made the second defence of his PFL belt.

Nurmagomedov's win marked his sixth world title defence in total after the Bellator title was rebranded by the PFL in 2025.

Following victory, Nurmagomedov paid tribute to training partner and UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev.

"This is from sparring with UFC legend and champion Islam Makhachev, that's how you can improve," said Nurmagomedov.

"Only one guy in the world pushes harder than me - Makhachev. That's why I follow him."

title: Mamdani's 'this is only the beginning' announcement cracking down on food delivery tips sparks outrage
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani faced viral backlash Thursday over a post claiming responsibility for increasing food delivery service tips.
fullText:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is facing fresh criticism after taking credit for a reported $104 million increase in delivery worker tips that critics say was made possible by legislation enacted before he took office and will likely only exacerbate cost of living issues in the city.

The criticism comes after Mamdani declared at a press conference Wednesday and in a social media post, "We've put $104 million back in delivery workers' pockets," citing changes to Uber Eats' and DoorDash's apps that made tipping more prominent.

"This is only the beginning," Mamdani wrote.

Those changes stem from a city law approved by the New York City Council before Mamdani became mayor. Former Mayor Eric Adams neither signed nor vetoed the measure, allowing it to become law after 30 days. The rules took effect in January under the Mamdani administration, which implemented and enforced the requirements.

Mamdani's 'Ration Shop' Grocery Plan Faces Blistering Economic Critique As Opponents Blast Socialist Policy

Before the law took effect, the New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection found that Uber Eats and DoorDash had hidden tip buttons and set default tips below 10%, contributing to a 79% decline in tips for delivery workers. The law required the companies to make tipping more prominent, and city officials say the resulting changes have since generated an estimated $104 million in additional tips.

Mamdani's office rejected the criticism that the mayor was taking credit for someone else's work, arguing that while the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection pushed for the reforms before he took office, the rules were implemented under his administration beginning Jan. 26.

"A law is only as good as its implementation," a spokesperson for Mamdani told Fox News Digital. "We have been intentional about enforcing the laws on the books so that we are putting money back into the pockets of working New Yorkers."

Conservatives and political commentators on social media quickly blasted Mamdani for the already high costs of goods and services in New York City, and some accused the mayor of taking credit for legislation that was born before his term.

"This guy is a fantastic lying politician," actor Michael Rapaport posted on X. "He had literally nothing to do with this. City Council passed the bill last August and 419 Eric Adams never signed it. 30 days the bill became law. It went into effect when Mamdani was in office. He just taking the credit."

Mamdani's Rent Freeze, Tax Hikes A 'One-two Wealth Destruction Punch,' Economists Warn

"In other words you are trying to say that you forced Uber and Doordash to make it that New Yorkers pay more for their food deliveries by having the default tip amount be a lot higher," conservative influencer account Leftism posted on X.

"Socialism 101 — have others pay for things and make as if it's your accomplishment."

"Coming soon — $50 avocado toast," Washington Free Beacon reporter Jon Levine posted on X.

"So you increased prices for your citizens?" National Review contributor Pradheep Shanker posted on X. "Congrats."

"What really happened," finance podcaster Joseph Carlson posted on X. "They forced delivery drivers to be paid minimum wage of $22/hr. This wage is paid by higher fees passed on to DoorDash or Uber customer. Since the customer was already paying these higher fees, these apps made tipping optional. Then New York required them to also be tipped on top of the higher fees.

"So now New York (residents) get to enjoy paying both a high base pay and a tip on top of it. The customer is double-paying for delivery. All of this cost is passed onto the New Yorker resident. They're paying more than the market demands for a product and service because of market manipulation."

title: NY Giants training camp report: Abdul Carter, Giants fans win the day
description: Fans treated to a spirited practice on second day of training camp in West Virginia.
fullText:
WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — Abdul Carter was dominant, Malik Nabers worked again, Kayvon Thibodeaux made an impact, and fans had fun on a beautiful West Virginia day as the New York Giants held their second practice of training camp.

Here are some of the winners and losers, as well as other takeaways.

Abdul Carter — Carter got the better of Andrew Thomas on Thursday, and let everybody know about it. [More about Carter’s big day]

Braxton Berrios — The veteran wide receiver/return man made several catches on Wednesday. He backed that up with another productive day on Thursday. Berrios is making an early impression in the competition for one of the final roster spots.

Dominic Zvada — There were no placekicking sessions in Thursday’s workout. On the final play of practice, though, Zvada walked on and drilled a 57-yard field goal after the ball had been clocked by backup quarterback Brandon Allen with :01 left on the clock. Score one for the undrafted free agent in his competition with Ben Sauls.

Leki Fotu — The journeyman defensive tackle had a disruptive day. Fotu had a tackle for loss and was in the backfield on a handful of other occasions.

Malik Nabers — The star wide receiver was on the field for a second straight day during individual drills. Every day that Nabers practices is a win for both him and the Giants.

Kayvon Thibodeaux — For the second straight day, Thibodeaux made an impact play. This time, Thibodeaux picked off a Jameis Winston pass at the line of scrimmage and took it to the house for a score. Thibodeaux has been working with the second team, but head coach John Harbaugh said he does not consider him a backup.

“He knows he’s going to play a bunch,” Harbaugh said. “We have three starters outside the linebacker. Those are all starting football players. Slice it how you want.”

Giants fans — This was the first practice attended by fans, and it happened on a gorgeous, sunny, comfortable day here in West Virginia.

Ben Barten — The Turk came for the undrafted free agent defensive tackle on Thursday, as he was cut and replaced on the roster by linebacker Anfernee Orji.

Theo Johnson — The third-year tight end, who has had an issue with drops over his first two seasons, dropped a pass for the second straight day.

Dante Miller — ‘Turbo’ fumbled after catching a short pass from Jameis Winston, with the result being a scoop-and-score for linebacker Micah McFadden.

One thing we have seen is that Harbaugh doesn’t believe in using a bunch of walk-through or install periods. After early special teams and individual work, the rest of practice the first two days has been full-speed 11-on-11 and 7-on-7 work. That is much more competitive and a faster pace than we have seen from the Giants in training camps during recent seasons.

As media members were walking to our station in a far corner of the Greenbrier practice facility, we saw rookie Sisi Mauigoa running a lap while waving at the crowd trying to fire up the fans. After practice, I asked Andrew Thomas what that was about.

“That was rookie duties,” Thomas said. “We made him go run around and fight the crowd. He did a good job.

“Probably made him some money, too. Probably about 10,000 Twitter followers.”

Can Nabers be as good or better after his knee injury than he was in 2024?

“I got extreme confidence in myself,” Nabers said. “I’m not going to put myself in any spot that I feel like I’m not going to be better than what I was before. So, I don’t see myself being what I was before. What I was before, what you all saw my rookie year, I felt like that was basic. I got high standards for myself. I know everybody has high standards for me also. But the standard that I hold myself to is very high. I feel like whatever that standard that I hold myself to, you’ll see or sooner or later.”

The Giants’ co-owner, who has been fighting a battle with cancer, made the trip to The Greenbrier.

title: Mets Reportedly Not Discussing Extension With Coveted Trade Candidate
description: The New York Mets could look to trade Clay Holmes this week
fullText:
The New York Mets are expected to be one of the most active sellers this week, leading up to the MLB trade deadline.

Among the players who could be dealt is pitcher Clay Holmes. After spending years as an All-Star reliever for the New York Yankees, Holmes signed a three-year, $38 million deal with the Mets as a starter. He had a solid first season as a starter, posting a 3.53 ERA.

This year, he had a 2.39 ERA through nine starts. Unfortunately, he fractured his fibula after taking a comebacker off the leg. He is currently on a rehab assignment, and during his last rehab start, scouts from the New York Yankees, Chicago White Sox, Philadelphia Phillies, Tampa Bay Rays, Rangers, Los Angeles Dodgers and Arizona Diamondbacks were present.

Teams are interested in him for sure. He has a $12 million player option for next season that he is likely to decline after establishing himself as a valuable starter. The Mets could try to keep him around after two strong seasons, but apparently they are not interested in that.

title: 'Change is inevitable' - Liverpool CEO on FSG, Iraola and consortium talks
description: Liverpool Billy Hogan talks to BBC Sport in New York about investment, transition and why FSG aren't done yet.
fullText:
With Liverpool stating that they have more than 26 million supporters in the USA, there is little surprise over why the Reds chose America as the destination for their pre-season tour.

This has been quite the summer for football here and Billy Hogan, CEO of Liverpool and Fenway Sports Group (FSG), insists the aim is to build on that after what has been a "super difficult year" for the club "for lots of different reasons."

Hogan is speaking to BBC Sport in New York ahead of Andoni Iraola's side taking on Wrexham at the famous Yankee Stadium on Wednesday evening at 19:30 local time, 00:30 BST.

However, for all the excitement around a new era on the pitch, it is events off the pitch that must be addressed first.

Last week, FSG, which owns Liverpool, confirmed that a consortium led by Amit Bhatia, a British-Indian millionaire businessman, was in talks over a strategic minority investment in the club. Those talks have been ongoing and there is a growing belief that a deal will be done.

"Look, John Henry (the principal owner) and FSG have always said that if there was an interest in an investment that would help the football club, then they would consider it. That was said many years ago and that remains the case here," Hogan tells BBC Sport.

"At this point, I wouldn't say anything different to the statement that a consortium led, managed and represented by Amit Bhatia has come forward and expressed an interest in a minority investment."

Hogan, who has been with FSG since they purchased Liverpool for £300m in 2010, does stress though that they are still very much committed to the project and that news of this development should not be seen as a sign of the company, which also owns the Major League Baseball franchise, Boston Red Sox, stepping away.

According to the Financial Times, a deal with the consortium led by Bhatia would value Liverpool at more than £4.5bn.

"There's a huge opportunity still," Hogan says. "This is the biggest and most popular sport in the world and we're one of the biggest clubs in the biggest league in the biggest sport in the world. So that's a great place for us to be. The Premier League has a tremendous amount of momentum behind it.

"We've definitely not peaked. We're in a good place to continue to grow and that's why everyone across both sides of the club, football and business and whether they kick a ball or not, is focused on driving the club forward and winning trophies.

"On the pitch, our goal every season is to win trophies. Off the pitch, our priority is to continue driving overall revenues and expand and build the club.

"We're really happy with the trajectory and direction of the club - we were fifth in the Deloitte Football Money League and had the highest revenue (£702m) in the Premier League.

"All of that investment, as has always been the case since 2010, goes back into the club. It's about running the club sustainably."

Who is potential investor Bhatia?

Consortium in talks to buy Liverpool minority stake

After a record summer spend last season of £450m, Liverpool were disappointing on the pitch.

Ultimately, that led to the sacking of Arne Slot at the end of the campaign. Senior players like Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate all left on free transfers too.

It has been a summer of change at Liverpool with Michael Edwards stepping down as FSG's CEO of football, primarily because plans of multi-club ownership were abandoned.

Meanwhile, Richard Hughes, Liverpool's sporting director, is linked with a move to Al Hilal in Saudi Arabia. There is certainly a question of stability.

"Transition and change is inevitable in football. In our case, with a new coach coming in, there's real excitement around Andoni's mindset and philosophy that supporters will really enjoy," says Hogan.

"That will take time but in terms of transition, I would send a message that we are in a very healthy place as a football club - the leadership from ownership is in a very steady place and we're looking forward to the next season and the season ahead."

Hogan insists that regardless of the personnel changes, the club model remains the same and they will continue to stick to their principles.

"It's important to keep in mind that last season, a considerable amount was invested but also generated in terms of sales of players going out," he says. "Over the course of FSG's stewardship, the investment has always been focused on doing what's best to put us in a place to win.

"Sometimes that means significant expense and other times it doesn't like in the summer of 2024 when there was only one addition (Federico Chiesa for £12.5m). It depends on where we are at the club and the improvements needed. Ultimately Mike Gordon, who is really our managing owner, will make those decisions."

There is an increased focus on the women's team too, who finished 11th in the WSL last season and haven't won the top-flight title since 2014.

"To be self-critical, that is probably an area that we maybe took our eye off the ball several years ago but we've changed that," says Hogan.

"We now have one of the best training centres at AXA Melwood, we are investing in the squad and we will approach the women's team the same way we approach the men's team - which is to run it sustainably. There's tremendous growth in the women's game and a huge opportunity going forward to really drive that."

Liverpool preparing opening bid for PSG's Barcola

It is still remarkable to think now that the club was on the verge of administration when FSG took over in 2010.

It hasn't all been plain sailing. As recently as this year, Hogan wrote to fans over ticket price increases. The club cut the size of their planned rise in ticket prices for the next couple of seasons after fan protests.

However, under FSG's stewardship, Anfield has been transformed, with two of the four stands developed in the last decade.

"Back when FSG acquired LFC, a number of similarities were drawn with Boston Red Sox and Liverpool and one of them was this idea of an iconic venue that truly sits in the community," says Hogan. "One of the things we're focused on now is making improvements in the footprint around Anfield the neighbourhood whether that's infrastructure or transport and getting people in on non-match days. We're proud of how we've expanded while keeping the soul but also modernising it in the way that's befitting of the football club.

"Football doesn't give you much time to sit back and reflect. What I would say I am most proud of is that the club is in such a positive and good financial position. If you go back to that point in 2010, the club was literally on the brink of bankruptcy. Now it has the right foundations underneath it. There's improvements across the infrastructure, the ability to stay at Anfield for the long-term and the stuff that doesn't always get headlines but are super important for the health of the club.

"Ultimately, it's about winning trophies and I wish we could win more but we've been fortunate to win a few.

"I think our supporters have had a great time and I often think about the fan parks at the Champions League finals - we lost a couple but just that joy and the memories and frankly the fun of it is what I look back from time to time. And it's something that everyone associated with Liverpool should be proud of because it happens together and we all want this club to be the best in the world."

After a torrid year for Liverpool, where better to start looking ahead than in New York, the city of dreams?

NEW YORK, July 28 (Reuters) - Bond investors said they are heading into this week's Federal Reserve policy meeting cautiously positioned as inflation uncertainty clouds the outlook for interest rates, favoring high-quality assets and avoiding large directional bets.

At 3.5%, U.S. consumer inflation slowed in June, but it remains well above the Fed's 2% target, while ongoing U.S.-Iran tensions, which escalated again this month, threaten another oil-driven rebound in price pressures.

With the policy ​outlook murky, portfolio managers do not see a compelling case for aggressively extending duration or taking on more credit risk. Duration measures the interest-rate sensitivity of a given bond holding.

Instead, they are emphasizing liquidity and flexibility as they wait for more inflation and employment data that could shed more light on the Fed's next move.

That caution was reflected in JPMorgan's latest Treasury Client Survey, which showed little change in investor positioning from a week earlier, with long, short and neutral positions all remaining near their four-week averages.

"I don't think that this is an environment that calls for meaningful positioning," said ‌Jason Granet, chief investment officer at BNY, who said he preferred ⁠smaller position sizes and tight risk management heading into Wednesday's decision. "There's a real chance it could go in either direction."

While Granet still expects rates to move higher over time, trying to monetize that view via a large wager on this week's decision is not prudent, he noted. Two weeks ago, ⁠he expected little fanfare from the meeting, but renewed inflation concerns tied mostly to energy price increases have since made the outcome less certain.

After starting the year pricing in two to three rate cuts, markets have swung dramatically in the other direction. U.S. rate futures on Monday priced in a 36% chance of a hike this week, according to the CME's FedWatch, up from 16% a week earlier, while showing ​43 ​basis points of increases by the end of 2026.

fullText:
Salamanca City Central says it is pausing project with Realbotix as it addresses concerns including data privacy

A New York school district has walked back plans to introduce a humanoid robot at its high school after the proposal sparked backlash from educators and community members.

The Salamanca City Central school district announced on 24 July in a social media post that its pilot project with Toronto-based tech company Realbotix had been put on hold “while we work through enhanced student data privacy agreements with the New York State Education Department and continue engaging with our community and stakeholders”.

“Ensuring that appropriate privacy protections are in place and incorporating input from our community are important parts of the process. We appreciate your patience and will share additional updates as they become available,” added the school district, which is located on the Seneca Nation reservation in upstate New York and serves a large Native American population.

The reversal came after widespread criticism of the program, which would have brought a humanoid robot named Sally to Salamanca high school. According to a Realbotix press release issued in June, the approximately $58,000 robot with silicone skin and brown hair was intended to use “natural conversation, facial expressions and real-time interaction to create engaging, hands-on learning experiences”.

“The robot aims to encourage student participation and provide early exposure to emerging technologies,” the company also said.

A little more than two years before Friday’s announcement, Realbotix acquired Simulacra, a Las Vegas-based company that manufactures sex dolls.

The New York State United Teachers union had condemned the plans calling for high schoolers to be taught by a humanoid robot.

“A robot built by a company associated with sex dolls has no business in our classrooms,” Melinda Person, the union president, said in a 23 July statement.

Person added: “Our students don’t need robots. They need real relationships with caring adults. Educators notice when students are struggling, celebrate when they succeed and help them discover who they can become. No robot can do that, no matter how lifelike its skin or specific its regional accent.”

Lacey Pihlblad, the president of the Salamanca Teachers’ Association and a teacher at the high school, also criticized the proposal, saying: “The Salamanca teachers’ union as a whole is concerned about the background of the company of Realbotix. We’re very concerned about the security of the software that they’re implementing, and whether or not the data will be stored, how it will be gathered, [and] the recording capabilities.”

Other educators also questioned why the pilot program was being launched at a school serving a large Native American population.

Speaking to the Guardian recently, Sierra May Abrams, a substitute teacher at Salamanca high school, said: “Out of all the schools in New York state, let alone in the US, they chose to experiment on Native American children yet again.”

Abrams alluded to the history of brutality at Native American boarding schools in the US and said: “Our culture is struggling to stay alive due to the impact of [that] and what they did to our elders. We live on the only reservation located in a city so it’s just absolutely insane that we’re the ones ‘testing it out’.”

Following the Salamanca district’s decision to pause the program, Realbotix’s CEO, Andrew Kiguel, told New York Focus: “We fully respect any decision the school makes and encourage thorough due diligence by all parties involved.

“We want the program to be demonstrably safe, fully district-approved, and strongly supported by teachers … We stand firmly behind [the program] as a supportive tool designed to assist teachers and students, not replace them.”

title: No, Miami isn’t more expensive than New York. But it may be less ‘affordable’
description: "Now they're having affordability issues, and I think that's really making people think twice about leaving New York," broker Michelle Griffith said.
fullText:
You may have seen the headline on your social media feeds this week, or some instance of it: Miami is now more expensive than New York City. The source of the headline is based on Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) data, which details the cost of living in Miami as greater than New York's for the first time ever.

How does Miami's cost of living compare to New York's?

What are the real estate price differences between cities?

What factors are driving Miami's affordability challenges?

How do job markets differ between Miami and New York?

The thing is, "expensive" is all relative. A locale's cost of living isn't a measure of raw prices—it's prices weighted against what local residents earn. The BEA finding doesn't mean that an apartment in Miami costs more than a comparable one in Manhattan. In fact, Manhattan's median listing price per square foot was $1,489 in May 2026, more than three times Miami-Dade County's $465, according to data retrieved via the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. What's changed is that Miami's prices have climbed further, relative to what the average Miami resident earns, compared to how New York's prices have climbed relative to what New Yorkers earn. And truth be told, both cities are viciously expensive.

That distinction also explains why the comparison misses how people actually live in each city. Cost-of-living indexes fold in categories that barely register for a Manhattan renter but hit Miami households hard, chief among them car ownership, along with rising insurance premiums, private school tuition and restaurant costs that have all climbed there over the past year. South Florida's consumer price index has risen 36% since 2019, more than any metro area tracked by the government, except Tampa. None of that has much to do with the price of Manhattan real estate.

Michelle Griffith, a broker at Douglas Elliman, has been fielding questions about the report since it published. It's really about that one word: affordability. "Affordability now in Miami, especially—and listen, I feel really badly for the people who were living in Miami [before this influx of new residents], and now all of a sudden the restaurant costs are going up, the transportation costs are going up, insurance costs are going up, rent is going up, tuition to send your kids to school is going up." That's a genuine problem for Miami residents, she added, but there isn't evidence that Miami has caught up to New York on the numbers that actually move real estate.

"When we really break down the numbers, the jobs are based in New York City," Griffith said. New York City's metro area added 86,800 jobs over the year through December 2025, more than double Miami's total and more than the combined job gains in Dallas, Philadelphia, and Atlanta, according to the NYCEDC's monthly economic snapshot. In contrast, Miami's metro area only added 42,600 jobs over the same 12-month stretch, according to BLS regional employment data, less than half of New York's total, despite Miami posting the faster percentage growth rate of the two metros.

In an 82-page complaint, Rana, who is of Nepali descent, added allegations that colleagues suggested he transact in rupees, and one texted that he should "run before we call ICEE {sic} on your family," referring to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
