title: Teachers decry plan for humanoid robot in New York high school
description: Robot from company that acquired sex doll maker to be introduced in school with large Native American population
fullText:
Robot from company that acquired sex doll maker to be introduced in school with large Native American population

A humanoid robot is being introduced as part of a pilot program, along with an AI teaching assistant, at Salamanca high school in Salamanca, New York, located on the Allegany territory of the Seneca nation.

Teachers have criticized the program, deeming it “inappropriate” and claiming it dehumanizes the profession with the introduction of human-like robots. Some local Native American residents have also criticized the pilot program, citing its implementation as “culturally tone deaf”.

The robot, named Sally, was purchased by the Cattaraugus county school district – which includes Salamanca high school – for $57,590. According to a presentation on the program, Sally will be a closed-loop system, but available virtually to students 24/7 for those with access, and offers personalized learning options.

The district will be the first in the US to deploy a humanoid robot and AI teaching assistant, according to a press release by Realbotix.

“The Salamanca pilot also includes deployment of a Realbotix M-Series humanoid robot, which uses natural conversation, facial expressions and real-time interaction to create engaging, hands-on learning experiences,” the press release states.

Realbotix, formerly Tokens.com, a Toronto-based company, purchased Simulacra, a Las Vegas-based company known for realistic sex dolls, for $16.7m in April 2024, marking a pivot for the company from crypto to humanoid robots.

Realbotix has denied ties to the sex doll company, and denied any inferences that the dolls – manufactured by Abyss Creations, a subsidiary of Realbotix – are related to the pilot program.

“The Salamanca teachers’ union as a whole is concerned about the background of the company of Realbotix. We’re very concerned about the security of the software that they’re implementing, and whether or not the data will be stored, how it will be gathered, are the recording capabilities,” said Lacey Pihlblad, president of Salamanca Teachers’ Association and a teacher at the high school.

“We would like to see the school district pause implementing the robot, pause implementing the software aspect of this AI technology until we can have more individuals weigh in.”

She said New York state is currently shifting away from too much technology in the classroom.

“There’s a growing consensus that indicates our students should be exposed to less technology. Placing a humanoid robot into the classroom to interact with our children, I believe, is a massive step in the wrong direction, and I believe that the majority of our teachers feel the same.” she added. “If we’re going to do something of this magnitude, I feel we need to make sure that we do it the correct way, and I’m not sure that that’s currently what’s in place.”

Pihlblad said the union was completing negotiations for a new union contract and intend to include protections around artificial intelligence.

Melinda Person, president of the New York State United Teachers, the parent union of the Salamanca Teachers’ Association, which represents teachers at the high school, told the Guardian that teachers across the state are concerned about the robot program.

“Our members in Salamanca and educators across the state are sounding the alarm that this is really inappropriate,” said Person. “I would say our initial reaction is this is kind of creepy.”

Person said it was “way out of the realm of what we should be doing in our schools”.

“The answer to the challenges in education is not more screens, it’s not more algorithms, not more robots. What we need in our schools right now are more caring adults and more human connection,” she said.

She said teachers were not anti-technology, but rather pro-child, and take positions based on whether something is beneficial for students.

“Putting a lifeless machine in front of students is a bad idea,” she said. “I would say a machine that the intention of it is to simulate a human relationship with young people who are just learning those skills of how to interact, how to be with their peers, how to solve conflicts, and putting a robot that looks like a human that will lead to the dehumanization of the profession of education, is exactly the wrong thing for us to be doing.”

Local residents have also criticized the selection of a high school with a significant Native American population to serve as the testing ground for humanoid robots in the classroom. Nearly 40% of the high school’s student body are Native Americans.

The Seneca nation declined to comment to the Guardian.

“Out of all the schools in New York state, let alone in the US, they chose to experiment on Native American children yet again,” said Sierra May Abrams, a substitute teacher at Salamanca high school and local resident. “Our culture is struggling to stay alive due to the impact of the Native American boarding schools and what they did to our elders. We live on the only reservation located in a city so it’s just absolutely insane that we’re the ones ‘testing it out’.”

Alyson Brown, a community health specialist and local resident and Seneca nation member who graduated from Salamanca, said several students have connections to the traumas of Native American boarding schools.

“Many students have connections to relatives who attended the Thomas Indian school located on our Cattaraugus territory. Many native families are viewing this pilot program as history repeating itself,” said Brown. “I see nothing positive to come from this being introduced in the classroom setting. I worry for the cognitive development of young minds in this exposure.”

A spokesperson for Realbotix did not comment on criticisms from teachers and Native American residents or the call for a pause from the Salamanca Teachers’ Association.

“Realbotix and Salamanca city central school district announced a limited pilot for fall 2026 involving Optio, an AI-powered educational assistant, and one new Realbotix M-Series humanoid unit,” the spokesperson said by email.

“The program is intended to complement, not replace, teachers by giving students supervised access to emerging AI and robotics tools as part of the district’s existing Stem [science, technology, engineering and mathematics] curriculum. The partnership also gives educators an opportunity to evaluate these technologies in a controlled classroom environment under district oversight.”

The Salamanca city central school district and superintendent Mark Beehler did not respond to multiple requests for comment.

The assistant commissioner of public affairs for the New York state department of education, JP O’Hare, said the agency had been in contact with the school district regarding its purchase of a robot “and has raised serious concerns about student privacy, appropriate safeguards, and the risk that the robot could be used to perform functions that should remain the responsibility of trained, qualified professionals.

“Technology can and should support educators and students, but it should not replace the human judgment or accountability essential to a safe and effective learning environment.”

title: Multiple Jets Players Will Start Training Camp With Injuries
description: Multiple New York Jets players including nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat will be starting training camp injured. The post Multiple Jets Players Will Start Training Camp With Injuries appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The New York Jets will deal with some adversity at the beginning of training camp.

Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic revealed that nose tackle T’Vondre Sweat “is going on the NFI list to start training camp with a hamstring injury. It’s not considered serious.”

“WR Tim Patrick and EDGE Tyler Baron will be placed on the PUP list at the start of camp as well. Patrick isn’t expected to be out long,” Rosenblatt added.

DT T'Vondre Sweat is going on the NFI list to start training camp with a hamstring injury. It's not considered serious, per source.

WR Tim Patrick and EDGE Tyler Baron will be placed on the PUP list at the start of camp as well. Patrick isn't expected to be out long, per…

— Zack Rosenblatt (@ZackBlatt) July 25, 2026

The team confirmed the news on social media. On Saturday, July 25, the Jets’ rookies reported for training camp. On Tuesday, July 28, the Jets’ veterans will report, and the first training camp practice will be held on Wednesday, July 29.

Sweat was placed on the NFI list to start camp. What does that mean?

The NFI list stands for “Non-Football-Injury or Illness,” and “it is used for players who suffered injuries or ailments outside of NFL activities,” according to NFL senior researcher Anthony Holzman-Escareno.

In other words, this means that Sweat got hurt somewhere between mandatory minicamp in the middle of June and training camp beginning here in late July.

The good news is that it isn’t considered serious, according to Rosenblatt. That is a huge sigh of relief.

Sweat is going to be a key straw that stirs the drink for the Jets’ defense. Especially when it comes to run defense, which is an area the team struggled in last season.

Patrick and Baron are dealing with an entirely different situation. They were both placed on the “active/physically unable to perform list,” according to Jets team reporter Ethan Greenberg.

“Players are placed on this list during training camp and count toward a team’s 90-man roster. Players can be removed from the list at any time during camp, but can’t be placed back on the list. Players on this list as of final roster cutdowns must be placed on the Reserve/PUP, released, traded or counted against the 53-man roster,” Holzman-Escareno wrote.

Patrick isn’t expected to be out long, according to Rosenblatt. He has a clear path to one of the top six wide receiver spots on the roster. Patrick will serve in the wise sage mentor role and as an occasional spot filler in case of emergency.

There was no update on Baron’s status from Rosenblatt.

Baron hurt his knee during the Week 14 contest against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, December 7, last season. Shortly after that game, he was placed on injured reserve, ending his rookie campaign. He could still be recovering from that issue.

This is troubling news for Baron. The former Miami product is 24 and will turn 25 during the 2026 season.

He appeared in six games, but didn’t make a start. Baron only appeared in 95 defensive snaps, per Pro Football Reference.

Before this news, Baron appeared to have long odds to make the Jets’ 53-man roster. This only complicates the path to making some noise. If he has any shot of changing his football destiny, Baron has to get back on the football field as quickly as possible.

fullText:
NEW YORK — After this disaster of a Mets season ends and the Mets start their postmortem, they’ll have to find out why Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor both suffered calf injuries, Jorge Polanco suffered an Achilles injury, and whether there is any correlation with their training program.

Soto was placed on the 10-day injured list Saturday with a Grade 2 left calf strain, his second time going on the IL this season with a calf strain. In April, Soto suffered a minor strain to his right calf in San Francisco, costing him only about three weeks of the season.

This time, he’ll be out for much longer, though the Mets declined to announce a tentative timeline. A typical timeline for this injury is 4-6 weeks, which would put him on track to return at some point in September. At that point, it might be more prudent to shut him down for the season, but interim manager Andy Green said he does expect Soto to return.

The club is having specialists review Soto’s MRI to determine a more precise timeline.

“Anticipation right now is it’s going to take longer than last time,” Green said Saturday ahead of the second game of a three-game series against the Los Angeles Dodgers. “He was out about three weeks last time, so it’s a little more significant than last time. It’s not what we were hoping for. He’s a guy we love having on the field; he’s a guy who loves to be on the field competing. We’ll be without him for a period of time now.”

Calf injuries and Achilles injuries tend to be related. The Mets have now had four of those injuries to three players this season, so it could simply be bad luck. It could also mean some of the training they’re having position players do is leading to a weakness in that area. It could also be both luck and training.

The club insists there are no commonalities they can find at the moment. Even if there is, they likely wouldn’t want to throw their training staff under the bus, and rightfully so. One positive with the Mets’ current culture is that guys aren’t afraid to report injuries. This is something they take pride in, and likely wouldn’t want to erode.

It’s also best not to anger or insult the medical staff, who still have jobs to do for the next few months. The team has consistently spoken highly of the club’s medical staff, Soto included.

Catcher Francisco Alvarez returned from meniscus surgery ahead of schedule this season, right-hander Clay Holmes is currently ahead of schedule with his rehab from a fractured fibula, and A.J. Minter had nothing but positive things to say after the way the team took care of him following his lat surgery last season, and his rehab into this season.

“It’s a frustrating set of circumstances,” Green said. “Definitely something we’ll reflect on and see if there’s anything that jumps out at this present moment. It feels unlucky to a degree, and it hasn’t been the same mechanism for each player, so when that’s the case, you’ve just got to look at each player and try to design their best path forward.”

The 27-year-old, $765 million outfielder has been one of the few bright spots this season, though that’s to be expected for a player of his caliber. His .947 OBP is the second-highest in baseball behind Houston’s Yordan Alvarez, and his .408 on-base mark is also No. 2 behind Alvarez. His 21 home runs lead the Mets by a large margin. Alvarez has hit the second-most with 12; Mark Vientos and Carson Benge have each hit 11, while Marcus Semien and Bo Bichette are behind them with 10.

Soto had been in the lineup as a DH more often than usual lately, especially over the last road trip with the Mets trying to mitigate the calf soreness. Without him, it will open up more DH at-bats for Polanco, who hasn’t been able to find his timing at the plate since coming off the IL earlier this month.

Limited to only nine games because of the way the Mets have to spread out at-bats, the switch-hitter has hit just .129 with two RBI, a walk and nine strikeouts in nine games.

“In the last week, Juan’s obviously taking quite a few of the DH at-bats, and I think that’s kind of stunted Polo’s ability to find some rhythm, so we’re going to try to get him back into a rhythm,” Green said. “He’s a guy we believe a lot in. Hopefully, as time goes on, we’ll get him to first base, and then we’ll see how the DH at-bats get divvied up at that point.”

Infielder Eric Wagaman was called up from Triple-A Syracuse to take Soto’s spot on the roster.

title: Fanatics Fest NYC: Inter's booth in the heart of New York
description: For the second consecutive year, Inter took centre stage at Fanatics Fest NYC, the biggest sports culture event in the United States, bringing to New York an experience that showcased the Club far bey...
fullText:
For the second consecutive year, Inter took centre stage at Fanatics Fest NYC, the biggest sports culture event in the United States, bringing to New York an experience that showcased the Club far beyond the football pitch.

The Nerazzurri booth welcomed thousands of visitors, offering a vibrant space where football, design, music and entertainment came together, once again highlighting the strength of the Inter brand on the international stage.

Inspired by contemporary industrial aesthetics and the concept of scaffolding, the booth drew on the shared urban language of Milano and New York. This design approach gave shape to the "Different Fields. Same Belonging." concept, the message behind the launch of the new Away Kit, portraying Inter as a Club capable of forging authentic connections across different worlds. Designed to express the Nerazzurri identity through a multifaceted visual language, the installation stood at the crossroads of sport, creativity and urban culture.

The booth took visitors on a journey through the Nerazzurri's past, present and future. The new kits, lifestyle collections, community-focused content, Inter's connection with the world of music and the Club's heritage brought the space to life, enhanced by a network of indoor and outdoor screens designed to make the experience even more immersive.

One of the booth's standout attractions was the display of the trophies from the Club's historic Double, attracting thousands of fans eager to admire up close two lasting reminders of an unforgettable season.

The fan activation also proved hugely popular. By answering a series of five questions, visitors were able to create their own Inter Emblem – a personalised symbol inspired by their identity and the way they experience their Nerazzurri passion. Each design was transformed into an exclusive pin, printed in real time and presented to fans at the end of the experience. The activation placed the community at its heart while also giving participants the chance to win a trip to Milano to discover some of the Club's most iconic locations, from San Siro to Inter HQ.

Over the course of the four-day event, the booth became one of Fanatics Fest's main attractions, welcoming Inter Vice President Javier Zanetti and Club Legend Christian Vieri, as well as participants in the Away Kit launch panel, including Dom Innarella, Chxrry, the Evening Elephants and many other Inter Friends.

The Nerazzurri booth proved to be a space that showcased every facet of Inter: a Club with a global voice, building connections between sport, culture and innovation through a shared sense of belonging.

title: Cam Schlittler strikes out 12 in Yankees win over Phillies, 1-0
description: Yankees star Cam Schlittler struck out 12 Phillies batters through 7.1 innings pitched as New York emerged 1-0 victors.
fullText:
The Yankees (58-45) beat the Philadelphia Phillies (56-48) in their road series opener on Friday night, 1-0, the final score.

-- Yankees first baseman Paul Goldschmidt opened the scoring with an opposite-field line drive solo homer, recording the team's first hit of the game in the fourth inning against Phillies southpaw Jesús Luzardo.

-- Yankees starting pitcher Cam Schlittler also allowed his first hit in the fourth inning, a double by Phillies slugger Kyle Schwarber with one out. Schlittler battled back to retire the next two batters and strand the runner in scoring position.

-- Goldschmidt came to the plate with the bases loaded and two outs in the fifth, but he softly grounded out and the score remained 1-0 Yanks.

-- Luzardo tossed seven innings, holding the Yankees to just one run, allowing three hits and one walk while striking out nine batters.

-- Not to be outdone by his counterpart, Schlittler was utterly dominant on the hill. He struck out every member of the Phillies batting order apart from Schwarber, racking up 12 strikeouts in the process. He finally slipped up with one man out in the eighth inning, allowing a single to J.T. Realmuto before promptly hitting Gabriel Rincones Jr. with a pitch. Schlittler was pulled having completed 7.1 innings, allowing three hits, walking zero batters, and throwing 99 pitches. Stalwart lefty Brent Headrick emerged from the bullpen to relieve the Yankee starter.

-- Edmundo Sosa roped a single into right field to load the bases on Headrick. After a lengthy battle, Trea Turner lined out to left field, but not deep enough to score Realmuto on a sacrifice. With two outs, Schwarber worked the count to 3-2, but Headrick got out of the jam with a groundout and held New York's one-run lead entering the ninth inning.

-- Lefty reliever José Alvarado plunked Ryan McMahon (who was pinch-hitting for Amed Rosario), but recovered by forcing Cody Bellinger into a groundout double play, holding the Yankees scoreless in the top half of the final frame.

-- David Bednar entered the 1-0 ballgame to face the heart of Philadelphia's order. Bednar struck out Bryce Harper swinging, got some assistance from Bellinger's leaping catch near the left-field wall for the second out, and got Alec Bohm to ground out to end the game. Bednar earned his 19th save of the season, and Schlittler earned his 10th win.

Among all American League pitchers who have accumulated at least 75 IP, Schlittler's 2026 ERA (2.07) is tops, and he's second-best in WHIP (0.93) behind Detroit Tigers ace Tarik Skubal.

The starting pitcher for the Yankees will be Ryan Weathers (4.40 ERA, 1.27 WHIP), while the Phillies have yet to name a starter.

title: Sabrina Ionescu 'didn't get invited' to defend WNBA 3-point crown
description: New York Liberty guard Sabrina Ionescu said she did not receive an official invitation to participate in this year’s WNBA three-point contest.
fullText:
New York Liberty star guard Sabrina Ionescu clarified on July 22 that she never officially received an invitation to defend her title in this year’s WNBA 3-point Contest and was surprised by reports that it was her choice not to participate.

In a press conference ahead of WNBA All-Star weekend, Ionescu said she was blindsided by media headlines suggesting she had declined an offer to participate. She emphasized her eagerness to compete whenever given the opportunity, but reiterated that she could not turn down an invitation she never received.

“I can’t decline an offer that I officially didn’t get invited to,” Ionescu said. “So I was pretty surprised to see that. Never got invited. Whether it's against Steph Curry or in the W, I always go out and try to beat my record every single time I step onto the court. I take pride in competing at the highest level, and I love representing the Liberty and the league in these contests. I just wanted to set the record straight – that rumor was simply false.”

"I can't decline an offer I never officially got invited to."

Sabrina Ionescu would've loved to beat her record in the three point contest, but the invite from the WNBA never came. pic.twitter.com/YRijofzzGR

— Sportico (@Sportico) July 22, 2026

Though she isn’t taking part in this year’s contest, Ionescu said she was excited to watch the event and to see who will become the new champion.

To Ionescu’s claim that she never received an invite, the WNBA responded with a statement saying, “Our general process is to reach out to agents to determine a player's interest, and some accept and some decline."

Ionescu is just the second player in league history to win multiple titles, winning in 2023 and 2025.

In 2025, she secured the title by scoring 30 of 40 points in the final round, surpassing Allisha Gray, who scored 22. Ionescu’s 30-point performance in 2025 came close to the league record of 37 points, which she set in 2023.

fullText:
In interview, billionaire says instead of running ‘Doge’ he should’ve ‘worked on my companies’ and shares extreme predictions

Elon Musk has admitted he became too consumed by politics during his volatile alliance with Donald Trump and his brief appointment as the president’s financial axman, running the so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge).

The world’s richest person, and briefly its first trillionaire after his SpaceX company floated on the New York stock exchange in June, made the confession in a wide-ranging interview with the Economist published on Thursday. He shared his positions on subjects from foreign wars to AI, and made a number of eye-opening predictions for the future.

“I got carried away, frankly,” Musk said of his relationship with the president, whom he helped get elected in 2024 with $200m in financial backing, then served during his controversial tenure as head of Doge, overseeing $150bn in “harmful” budget cuts and forcing tens of thousands of people out of federal jobs.

The owner of Tesla did not expand on the statement, but appeared cognizant of the impact of his dalliance with the levers of power in Washington DC.

In December, he offered in a podcast with Katie Miller, wife of Trump’s White House adviser Stephen Miller, that his wrecking-ball approach to the federal government had been only partially successful, and that given the opportunity he probably wouldn’t do it again.

“I think instead of doing Doge, I would have basically worked on my companies,” he said at the time.

Talking to the Economist, however, he appeared to relish the attention his political involvement had garnered, and the influence he believed he exerted. “People don’t realize that what I’m saying will come to pass,” he said, the outlet referring to Musk – at least in his own mind – as a modern-day Cassandra.

The interview, a 90-minute conversation for the publication’s video platform The Insider, recorded at a Tesla factory in Texas, was Musk’s first since the SpaceX flotation, in which his personal wealth briefly topped $1.25tn before dropping back to a relatively penurious $750bn.

He reflected on moving from “exhilaration to terror” in a single day, but was not referring to the SpaceX share price. Instead, he was talking about artificial intelligence, which he believes will ultimately render work by humans “optional”.

AI systems and robots will eventually handle most digital and physical jobs, he said, and the merger of his own AI venture with SpaceX will allow him to develop systems to perform cognitive tasks such as software programming while Tesla manufactures humanoids.

Musk, the Economist said, plans to power his AI venture with datacenters in space, which experts have warned will be “catastrophic” for Earth.

Within five years, Musk said, AI intelligence systems may surpass the sum of all human intelligence. Within 10 years, robots in the workplace will help usher in an era of such “amazing abundance” that money will become meaningless.

It was, however, Musk’s political views, and predictions, that were perhaps the most contentious parts of the interview. The UK, a country he has not visited for years, but whose politics, especially on immigration and race, have become a recent obsession, will become engulfed in a civil war within 20 years, he claimed.

Asked if he was anti-Muslim, Musk attacked the questioner, a policy of diversion similar to that which has served Trump well, and which he has employed previously, notably calling the Guardian “irrelevant” when it decided to withdraw from his “toxic” social media platform X.

“I’m against rape and murder. I’m against the imposition of rules and laws that are contrary to what we’ve come to accept in the west,” he said. “It’s a crying shame that traditional media, like you, don’t recognize this.”

He described the media’s characterization of Europe’s far right as “false, misleading and nonsense”, and argued that it was made up of “normal people” seeking safe cities, secure borders and sensible spending, the Economist said.

In an analysis piece accompanying the interview, the outlet acknowledged that Musk was a divisive figure. “His political views, disseminated to his 240m followers on X, strike many as plain-speaking and strike many more, including The Economist, as plainly bigoted,” it wrote.

“But he is also one of a handful of men who are pioneering AI and who thereby have an outsize influence on its trajectory. When he speaks, he reflects the debates they are having. His datacentres in space could power AI’s future.

“For all his political polemics, he has a record of being right about technology in fields such as electric cars, rockets and satellite communications that confounded other engineers and entrepreneurs.”

Another Musk prediction: after AI destroys jobs, there may need to be a large-scale wealth redistribution to create “universal high income” for humans.

He said he would be willing to pay “trillions in tax” then, conversely, argued that money will become irrelevant inside 10 years. In which eventuality, he said, governments should “issue people cheques”, because, he said, amid an infinite supply of goods and services produced by machines, deflation will be a bigger problem than inflation.

He also shared thoughts about the Ukraine war, in which his Starlink satellites have been used to help that country’s military against Russia’s aggression. Despite this, Musk said any peace deal should include territorial gains for Russia.

The interview concluded with an assessment by Musk of his achievements and ambitious current projects, in AI and in space, a field in which he has also made a number of bold predictions. He said in 2024 that humans could set foot on Mars by 2028 (currently Nasa is targeting 2028 for a return to the moon, which many analysts think is unlikely).

The universe, Musk said, according to the Economist, could be a computer simulation created by aliens. “The things I’m doing are so preposterous that it’s hard to believe they’re real,” he said.
